  • Cache

Cache

Tess can cache public API responses in a server speaking the Redis protocol: Valkey, Redis, KeyDB, Dragonfly, or a managed service. Use the one your team already runs. The cache is optional: with TESS_CACHE=none (the default) nothing changes.

TESS_CACHE=valkey                     # valkey, redis, keydb or dragonfly
TESS_CACHE_URL=redis://valkey:6379    # rediss:// for TLS; redis://user:password@host:6379/0
TESS_CACHE_TTL_SECS=60
TESS_CACHE_PREFIX=tess:               # to share one server between installs

Choosing a server​

They all work the same way for Tess: it only uses GET, SET … PX, INCR, PUBLISH and SUBSCRIBE. TESS_CACHE names the server in the logs and in /health.

ServerTESS_CACHECompose profileLicenseNotes
Valkey 8valkeycacheBSD 3-ClauseLinux Foundation fork of Redis 7.2. The default here.
Redis 8rediscache-redisRSALv2, SSPLv1 or AGPLv3Redis 6 and 7 work too.
KeyDB 6.3keydbcache-keydbBSD 3-ClauseMultithreaded fork of Redis. Its last release is from 2023.
Dragonfly 2dragonflycache-dragonflyBSL 1.1Multithreaded, Redis-compatible; needs 256 MiB per thread.
Managed servicethe engine's nameSee below.

Licenses are given for information: check them with each vendor. All four are tested with Tess (TESS_TEST_CACHE_URL=… cargo test -p tess-cache).

Not supported: cluster mode (Redis Cluster, ElastiCache "cluster mode enabled") and Sentinel. Use a single primary endpoint: a cache needs no sharding at this size, and a replica failover only empties it.

Examples​

Docker Compose​

docker-compose.yml has a service for each server, in its own profile, with no persistence, a memory limit (CACHE_MAXMEMORY, default 256mb) and LRU eviction. Pick one:

# Valkey
TESS_CACHE=valkey     TESS_CACHE_URL=redis://valkey:6379       # docker compose --profile cache up -d
# Redis
TESS_CACHE=redis      TESS_CACHE_URL=redis://redis:6379        # docker compose --profile cache-redis up -d
# KeyDB
TESS_CACHE=keydb      TESS_CACHE_URL=redis://keydb:6379        # docker compose --profile cache-keydb up -d
# Dragonfly
TESS_CACHE=dragonfly  TESS_CACHE_URL=redis://dragonfly:6379    # docker compose --profile cache-dragonfly up -d

scripts/init-env.sh --cache redis (or valkey, keydb, dragonfly) writes these settings and prints the matching command.

Your own server​

The services above, as docker run commands (any recent version works):

docker run -d --name valkey    -p 6379:6379 valkey/valkey:8-alpine \
  valkey-server --save "" --appendonly no --maxmemory 256mb --maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru

docker run -d --name redis     -p 6379:6379 redis:8-alpine \
  redis-server --save "" --appendonly no --maxmemory 256mb --maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru

docker run -d --name keydb     -p 6379:6379 eqalpha/keydb:latest \
  keydb-server --save "" --appendonly no --maxmemory 256mb --maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru

docker run -d --name dragonfly -p 6379:6379 --ulimit memlock=-1 docker.dragonflydb.io/dragonflydb/dragonfly:v2.0.2 \
  --cache_mode=true --maxmemory=256mb --proactor_threads=1 --dbfilename=

With a password (requirepass, or an ACL user), put it in the URL: redis://:password@host:6379, or redis://user:password@host:6379. A database number goes at the end: redis://host:6379/2.

Managed services​

ServiceTESS_CACHETESS_CACHE_URL
Amazon ElastiCache (Valkey or Redis OSS, cluster mode disabled)valkey / redisrediss://:AUTH_TOKEN@master.my-cache.xxxxxx.euw1.cache.amazonaws.com:6379 (primary endpoint, with in-transit encryption)
Amazon MemoryDBvalkey / redisNot supported: MemoryDB always runs in cluster mode.
Azure Cache for Redisredisrediss://:ACCESS_KEY@my-cache.redis.cache.windows.net:6380
Google Cloud Memorystore (Valkey or Redis)valkey / redisredis://10.0.0.3:6379 (private IP; rediss:// with in-transit encryption)
Upstashredisrediss://default:PASSWORD@my-db.upstash.io:6379
Redis Cloudredisrediss://default:PASSWORD@redis-12345.c1.eu-west-1-2.ec2.redns.redis-cloud.com:12345

TLS (rediss://) checks the server certificate against the public CA roots.

What is cached​

CachedKey
GraphQL queries by anonymous visitors (public reads, PUBLISHED content)✔query, operation name, variables
Translation files served at /i18n/{format}/{file}✔format, file
Requests with a token or session, mutations, responses with errors✘

Responses carry an X-Tess-Cache header: HIT, MISS, or BYPASS when the cache server is unavailable.

Drafts are never cached: anonymous visitors can only read published content, and signed-in requests always go to the database, so editors and previews always see the latest version.

Invalidation​

You never purge the cache by hand. Every change invalidates it:

  • Content: creating, updating, publishing, unpublishing or deleting an entry (from the admin UI, the API, MCP, plugins or imports), a change to a content model or component, and any successful mutation.
  • Translations: any change to languages, keys or texts.

Invalidation is instant and costs one command: each scope has a generation counter that is part of every key. Changing it makes all older entries unreachable, and they expire on their TTL.

Several instances​

With a cache server, all Tess instances share the cache: a response cached by one is served by the others, and a change on any instance invalidates it for all.

The server also carries the content model changes (pub/sub): when one instance changes a model, the others rebuild their GraphQL schema at once instead of after the TESS_SCHEMA_REFRESH_SECS delay.

Sizing and eviction​

Give the server a memory limit and let it evict the least recently used keys: --maxmemory 256mb --maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru (Valkey, Redis, KeyDB), or --cache_mode=true --maxmemory=256mb (Dragonfly). volatile-lru works too. Persistence is not needed: an empty cache only means a few slower requests.

Any eviction policy is safe. If a server evicts an invalidation counter, Tess restarts it from the current time, never from a value it had before, so entries cached earlier can't come back.

TESS_CACHE_TTL_SECS is capped at half of TESS_MEDIA_URL_TTL_SECS and of TESS_ID_TTL, so cached responses never contain expired file URLs or ids.

When the cache server is down​

Tess keeps working without it. Requests skip the cache (X-Tess-Cache: BYPASS) and a warning is logged. After a failure Tess waits 5 seconds before trying again, so requests don't wait on an unresponsive server. The cache is used again as soon as the server answers, and the other instances' schemas are refreshed in case a change was missed.

Memory​

TESS_CACHE=memory keeps the cache in the process (at most TESS_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES responses). It only suits a single instance: other instances would serve stale responses until the TTL.

AWS Lambda​

Use a cache server (ElastiCache or Upstash) so that all concurrent Lambda instances share the cache and its invalidation.
